selected_experts.reason: Verify the fish's identity as a tench (Tinca tinca) by checking for key taxonomic features: small deeply embedded cycloid scales, olive-green to golden-bronze coloration, small head with blunt downturned mouth, two short barbels at each corner, small eyes with reddish-orange iris, short rounded dorsal fin, truncate to slightly emarginate caudal fin, and complete lateral line.
Locate the tench in the image to identify specific body parts (head, mouth, barbels, eyes, dorsal fin, caudal fin, lateral line) for detailed anatomical verification.
Assess the overall image quality, focusing on the texture of the fish's skin (should be smooth and slimy/mucous-coated) and the clarity of its features (scales, fins, lateral line).

Verify the spatial relationship between the man and the fish, ensuring the fish is being held naturally and not floating or fused with the man's hands. Also check the background (grass, trees, net) for perspective and depth consistency.
Check for boundary integrity of the fish, ensuring no parts are floating or blurred, and that the fish is clearly separated from the background and the man's hands.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay special attention to the fish's barbels (should be two short ones at each corner of the mouth), the shape and ray count of the dorsal and caudal fins, the presence and visibility of the lateral line, and the smooth, slimy texture of the skin. Ensure the man is holding the fish in a natural position without any anatomical distortions in his hands or the fish's body.
